description: Filter whose focus frequency sweeps cyclically over a range. Pinned to submode 2 (BAND-PASS) — most musically useful sweep behavior for textured source material. 'filter sweeping' has four filter-shape sub-modes (notch, bandpass, lowpass, highpass); other shapes can be added as separate curated entries later.
musical_use: Time-varying bandpass that sweeps between lofrq and hifrq at sweepfrq Hz. Classic wah/sweep effects, automatic spectral animation, vowel-formant-like motion. The 'phase' parameter controls where in the sweep cycle playback starts, useful for stylistic choices (rising vs falling at the entry).

acuity.description: Filter acuity. Smaller values give a tighter (narrower) filter. Rule of thumb from CDP docs: if acuity = (1/3)^n, gain = (2/3)^n.

gain.description: Overall gain on output. See the acuity rule-of-thumb above.

sweepfrq.description: Frequency of the sweep itself, in Hz — the focus oscillates lofrq<->hifrq at this rate. For a single rising pass across the whole file, set sweepfrq = 1/(2*infiledur) with phase = 0 (e.g. a 10 s file -> 0.05 Hz; a 7.2 s file -> ~0.069 Hz); use phase = 0.5 for a single falling pass. Read the input's duration first (it is not known to this tool). NOTE: CDP's own usage banner mis-states this as 'infiledur/2', which would give many sweeps -- that is a CDP doc error.

tail.description: Decay tail duration appended after the input ends. NOT in CDP's HTML manual (banner-only parameter); empirically, omitting -t makes the r8 binary append a ~1 s tail anyway. The engine therefore always emits -t explicitly (default 1.0) so the output duration is deterministic and the duration model (indur + tail) matches what CDP produces. Set 0.0 to suppress the tail.

phase.description: Start of sweep: 0 = lofrq rising, 0.5 = hifrq falling, 1 = lofrq. Default 0.25 = midfrq rising.

examples.description: Bandpass sweep between 200 Hz and 4 kHz at 1 Hz, starting mid-range and rising.
examples.expected_use: Animate a sustained or looped texture with a slow, audible spectral sweep.

known_issues: The -t tail parameter exists only in the binary's usage banner, not the CDP HTML manual. With -t omitted the r8 binary appends a default tail (observed: exactly +1.00 s on a 4.00 s input, 2026-07-14 manual QA), which made the previous 'static' duration model under-predict. Pinned by the CDP-gated regression in test_curation_formulas.py.
